elements.element: Customer has the right to terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly provides that “Ono as Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer’s termination-for-convenience right is available throughout the Agreement term without a commencement time-gate.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 13.2 contains no First Commercial Sale or other commencement condition on Ono’s right.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right on 30 days’ advance notice.
Customer’s termination-for-convenience notice must be written.
Upon Customer’s termination for convenience, Vendor must refund prepaid fees to Customer.
elements.evidence: The added operative language states that, upon termination by Ono under Section 13.2, “Array shall pay Ono a ... refund of prepaid fees.”

elements.element: The refund of prepaid fees must be prorated for the period following the effective date of termination.
elements.evidence: The refund is expressly described as “pro-rata” and applies to prepaid fees “for the period after the effective date of termination.”

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 grants the convenience right only to Ono. Array’s only stated early-termination right is for material breach under Section 13.3, not convenience.

elements.element: Customer has the right to terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly grants Ono as Customer a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer’s termination-for-convenience notice period is between 60 and 90 days.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause requires only 30 days’ advance notice, which is outside the specified 60–90 day fallback range.

elements.element: If an early-termination fee applies to Customer’s termination for convenience, it does not exceed three months’ fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed, so the conditional cap is satisfied; the clause instead requires Array to provide a prorated refund.

elements.element: If Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right, it may be exercised only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: the rendered termination provisions grant Array no termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: If Vendor has a termination-for-convenience right, it requires 90 days’ notice.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because Array has no termination-for-convenience right; Section 13.3 addresses termination for breach only.

result.reason: The operative redline fully reaches the preferred position: Ono has an ungated convenience right on 30 days’ written notice, receives a prorated refund of prepaid fees, and Array has no convenience right. The fallback is not independently satisfied because its required Customer notice range is 60–90 days, while the clause uses 30 days. The edits are substantively targeted and preserve the term and breach-termination provisions. Drafting quality is weakened by retaining the requirement that a no-cause termination notice include a rationale and by placing the refund sentence after Section 13.3 rather than within Section 13.2.
